title: Less Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Less course.

entries.name: Build your first Less file
entries.summary: Less is a CSS helper language. A compiler translates its extra features into the CSS that browsers already understand.

entries.name: Store a colour in a name
entries.summary: Less variables start with @. A variable lets you reuse a value such as a colour or a spacing size.

entries.name: Nest child styles
entries.summary: A nested selector chooses an element inside another element.

entries.name: Style the current element
entries.summary: The & sign repeats the parent selector. It helps add a state to the same element rather than choosing one of its children.

entries.name: Reuse a mixin
entries.summary: A mixin is a group of style choices you can insert into another rule.

entries.name: Pass a mixin value
entries.summary: A mixin can accept a value, so one recipe makes several kinds of frame.

entries.name: Calculate space
entries.summary: Less can calculate a size from other sizes.

entries.name: Split a style file
entries.summary: An import brings another Less file into the build.

entries.name: Guard a recipe
entries.summary: A guard is a rule that decides whether a mixin should run.

entries.name: Change a colour value
entries.summary: Less has colour functions. A function takes a colour and calculates another colour from it.

entries.name: Insert a name into a selector
entries.summary: Interpolation puts a variable value inside a selector name.

entries.name: Combine a card and a screen rule
entries.summary: A media query chooses styles for certain screen sizes.
